terms.short: A fast, cheap classifier from TypeSafe AI that answers yes/no and multiple-choice checks with probabilities — it doesn't write text.
One quick call that asks every check on a route about an answer at once, with probabilities, before or while the answer reaches your user.
An LLM judge that splits an answer into claims and checks each one against your documents. It runs after delivery, on flagged answers and a small sample.
Deterministic rules that run without a model call, such as a number, date or link in the answer that isn't in your documents.
The documents your app already gave the model: system-prompt documents, attached context, tool results.
Whether every fact in the answer is stated in, or directly implied by, your documents.
Your documents say something in the answer is false — stronger than a fact your documents simply don’t mention.
We only judge facts against your documents. None were found, so we didn't guess.
One check, such as groundedness or refusal, written as a question the fast check answers on every request.
A group of requests, matched by header, path, model or key, that share one policy.
The per-route rules that decide what happens to a risky answer: observe, flag, block or fallback.
Check answers and record what would have happened, without changing any response.
Deliver the answer and tell your app it looks risky, through X-TrustAgent-* response headers.
Replace a risky answer with a safe message before your user sees it. Blocking needs two checks to agree.
Ask the model again with only your documents, check the new answer, and deliver it if it passes.
What happens when a check can't finish: fail open delivers the answer unchecked; fail closed blocks it.
The mode a route really runs in right now. A Block route acts as Flag until blocking is possible, for example until its checks are calibrated or its streams are buffered.
Blocking needs two checks to agree, so one noisy check can't block an answer.
A number from 0 to 1 where higher means riskier. Shown as Low, Elevated or High risk.
Tuning thresholds on your own labelled traffic so 'risk 0.9' really means about 9 in 10.
Your verdict on an answer: it has the problem a check looks for, or it is fine. Labels calibrate checks.
The exact Jev version that answered. A new version can shift scores, so blocking pauses until you re-check.
A check in shadow runs on every request and shows up in traces, but never changes what your user receives.
A small random share of all answers that always gets a deep audit, so the hallucination rate isn't skewed by what was flagged.
The share of uniformly sampled answers in which the deep audit found unsupported or contradicted claims. Shown with a confidence interval once enough samples exist.
An optional add-on that searches documents you uploaded when a request carries none of its own.
Produced by our own benchmark runs or your own traffic.
Our arithmetic from stated assumptions, not a measurement.
Published by an independent source; linked and dated.
Published by the model's maker or distributor; linked and dated.
Produced by mock checks and a mock judge, not by a real model.
A question the fast check answers with one probability that the statement is true.
A question the fast check answers with a probability for each option.
A question the fast check answers with a probability for each level of a scale.
